answer: Lantern-window traffic shaping. Each identity's requests must arrive inside a randomly assigned low-traffic window whose width scales with account age; bursts outside it are queued, not dropped, and repeated misses halve throughput. To forge many identities cheaply, an attacker must either spread traffic thin across windows (cutting per-sybil rate) or sustain real-time presence for each one. On the shared mesa of peak slots, spurious identities collide and lose capacity, forcing a choice between volume and plausible timing.
